---
title: "Country inputs"
---

The public arguments follow the English Input 1-8 instructions in the workbook.
You supply those leaves; the package evaluates the engine sheets internally.

| Workbook group | What you are setting | Typical `compute_*` arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input 1-2 | Country, first projection year, discount rate, external/domestic definition, contingent liabilities, REER overvaluation | `country`, `first_projection_year`, `discount_rate`, `external_domestic_debt_definition`, `input_1_rer_overvaluation`, `contingent_liability_*` |
| Input 3 | Macro-debt history and projections | `input3_input_3_macro_*`, `input3_old_debt_service`, `input3_new_disbursements`, domestic existing-debt stocks and flows |
| Input 4 | External financing terms and disbursements | `input4_interest_rate`, `input4_grace_period`, `input4_loan_maturity`, `input4_disbursements`, `input4_instrument_names`, blend settings |
| Input 5 | Domestic financing terms and GFNS adjustments | `input5_grace_period`, `input5_interest_rate_on_domestic_debt`, `input5_maturity`, `input5_gfn_share` |
| Input 6 | Standardized and tailored stress options | `input6_tailored_tests_enabled`, `input6_commodity_group_relevant`, standard-test mode and thresholds |
| Input 7-8 | Residual financing and SDR | `input8_sdr_interest_rate`, `input8_sdr_stock` |
| Customized sheets | Optional public / external alternative paths | `customized_public_*`, `customized_external_*` |

Do not treat `Macro-Debt_Data`, `Ext_Debt_Data`, `PV_Base`, `PV Stress`, or
`Chart Data` as places to enter assumptions. Those sheets are outputs of the
same formulas the `compute_*` functions already run.

# Use the workbook's labels

Country names, instrument codes, and commodity-group titles are workbook
strings. ISO codes and lowercase names are out of domain.

```{python}
from lic_dsf_2025_08_12 import data

print(data.COUNTRY_DEFAULT)
print(data.FIRST_PROJECTION_YEAR_DEFAULT)
print(data.DISCOUNT_RATE_DEFAULT)
print(data.EXTERNAL_DOMESTIC_DEBT_DEFINITION_DEFAULT)
print(data.INPUT6_TAILORED_TESTS_ENABLED_DEFAULT)
print(data.INPUT_1_RER_OVERVALUATION_DEFAULT)
```

Country names are a closed workbook list. Inspect the axis before you guess at
a spelling:

```{python}
print(len(data.REF_AREA_AXIS_3.keys))
print(data.REF_AREA_AXIS_3.keys[:8])
print("Ghana" in data.REF_AREA_AXIS_3.keys)
print("BGD" in data.REF_AREA_AXIS_3.keys)
```

Different arguments can use different country lists. If a call raises
`ValueError: ... out of domain`, the rejected value is not in *that*
argument's axis, even if it appears somewhere else in `data`.

# Inspect a series before you overwrite it

Input 3 GDP is a `TIME_PERIOD` series covering history and the projection.
Index it by calendar year, not by position:

```{python}
gdp = data.INPUT3_INPUT_3_MACRO_GROSS_DOMESTIC_PRODUCT_US_DOLLARS_DEFAULT
years = gdp.domain.axes[0].keys
print(years[0], years[-1], len(years))
print(gdp[2013])
print(gdp[2024])
```

Input 4 interest rates are keyed by instrument, not by year:

```{python}
rates = data.INPUT4_INTEREST_RATE_DEFAULT
print(rates.domain.axes[0].keys[:6])
print(rates["IMF"])
print(rates["Eurobond"])
```

Input 6 commodity relevance is four Yes/No flags:

```{python}
relevant = data.INPUT6_COMMODITY_GROUP_RELEVANT_DEFAULT
for (commodity,), flag in relevant.items():
    print(f"{flag:3}  {commodity}")
```

# Revise one coordinate

Copy the template series and replace the coordinates you actually changed.
`collect` rebuilds the typed series over the same required domain:

```{python}
import inspect

from lic_dsf_2025_08_12.api import compute_tailored_stress_commodity_price_applicable


def template_inputs(compute):
    return {
        name: getattr(data, f"{name.upper()}_DEFAULT")
        for name in inspect.signature(compute).parameters
    }


precious = "2) Precious metal (e.g., gold, silver, platinum, etc.)"
base = data.INPUT6_COMMODITY_GROUP_RELEVANT_DEFAULT
all_no = type(base).collect(
    (coord, "No")
    for coord, _value in base.items()
)

inputs = template_inputs(compute_tailored_stress_commodity_price_applicable)
inputs["input6_commodity_group_relevant"] = all_no
print("all groups No:", compute_tailored_stress_commodity_price_applicable(**inputs))

only_precious = type(base).collect(
    (coord, "Yes" if coord == (precious,) else "No")
    for coord, _value in base.items()
)
inputs["input6_commodity_group_relevant"] = only_precious
print("precious only:", compute_tailored_stress_commodity_price_applicable(**inputs))
```

The applicability flag can stay on when trade shares still meet the commodity
test, even after you flip every Input 6 group to `No`. That is the same
mechanical rule as Input 6 plus the commodity rows on Input 3.

# Blank projection cells

Some Input 3 and customized-scenario cells are blank in the template. Those
blanks are OFFSET placeholders, not missing economist parameters. Leave them
as `None` unless you are filling a real entry cell. Filling every blank with
zero will not reproduce the workbook.
